# 0056: Release SBOMs are generated by a digest-pinned syft container in the build job and attested in the attest job

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-05
- **Source:** Issue #119
- **Supersedes:** — (amends [0054](0054-release-provenance-attestations-from-a-secret-free-job.md), option 4 and
  the last sentence of its *Decision*, "No SBOM is published"; the rest of 0054 stands)

## Context

Record 0054 added SLSA build provenance attestations for `vandox-agent-linux-amd64` and the image
`networlddev/vandox` in a separate `attest` job of `.github/workflows/release.yml`, and left the optional SBOM
out: every way of generating one that it considered brought a third-party tool or an image not pinned by
digest into the release pipeline, against security area 13 (every action pinned by commit SHA, every base
image by digest). Issue #119 asks for an SBOM (SPDX or CycloneDX) for the binary and the image, attested with
`actions/attest` (`sbom-path`) in the `attest` job, with a generator pinned by SHA or digest and
checksum-verified, no cache, no `${{ }}` in `run:`, the `attest` job keeping only `id-token: write` and
`attestations: write`, and the verification documented.

Facts this decision rests on (checked on 2026-10-05):

- `actions/attest` at the pinned commit `1e69f48acb82d1966a394da916b4c1698aa569d6` (v4.2.2) has the input
  `sbom-path` (SPDX or CycloneDX JSON, at most 16 MB; not combinable with `predicate*`). For SPDX it sets the
  predicate type `https://spdx.dev/Document/v<version>` from the document's `spdxVersion` (`SPDX-2.3` gives
  `https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`); for CycloneDX always `https://cyclonedx.org/bom` (`src/sbom.ts`).
- `gh attestation verify` checks `https://slsa.dev/provenance/v1` by default; another predicate type needs
  `--predicate-type`. With `--format json` it prints the verified statements, including the predicate, which
  for an SBOM attestation is the SBOM document itself.
- syft (Anchore) catalogs Go modules from a binary's embedded build information (present despite `-s -w`) and
  Debian packages from a distroless image's `/var/lib/dpkg/status.d/`, and reads an image from a
  `docker save` tarball (`docker-archive:`) without a Docker daemon or network. It is published as a
  multi-arch image `ghcr.io/anchore/syft` (and as `anchore/syft` on Docker Hub). Anonymous Docker Hub lookups
  from shared addresses hit `429 Too Many Requests` (observed while planning this change); `ghcr.io` is
  GitHub's own registry.
- A pull by `name:tag@sha256:<digest>` ignores the tag and is verified by the Docker daemon against the
  digest: the content is checksum-verified by construction.
- Dependabot's `github-actions` and `gomod` entries do not read image references inside `run:` scripts.
- A tool dependency in `go.mod` is part of the main module's build list: its requirements can raise the
  versions of modules that the release binaries link (minimal version selection).

## Options considered

1. **Generator**
   - *`anchore/sbom-action`, pinned by commit SHA*: the action itself is pinned, but it downloads a syft
     binary at run time (and may keep it in the tool cache), so the generator that actually runs is neither
     pinned by our digest nor checked against our checksum. Rejected.
   - *BuildKit `--sbom` / `--attest type=sbom`*: the scanner image can be pinned by digest, but it needs
     `buildx` with a `docker-container` driver or the containerd image store, and the attestation manifests
     do not survive the classic `docker save`/`docker load` path that 0037 uses to push exactly the verified
     image; it covers the image only, not the binary. Rejected.
   - *A Go SBOM generator as a `tool` dependency in `go.mod`* (e.g. `cyclonedx-gomod`, or syft's own module):
     pinned and checksum-verified through `go.sum`, updated by Dependabot. Cons: its requirements join the
     main module's build list and can move versions of modules linked into `vandox-agent`/`vandoxd`; syft's
     module tree is very large; `cyclonedx-gomod` sees only Go modules, so the image SBOM would miss the
     distroless Debian packages. Rejected.
   - *A hand-written generator* from `go version -m` and `dpkg` status files: no third-party code, but the
     project would maintain SPDX/CycloneDX correctness and package URLs itself. Rejected.
   - *The syft release binary*, downloaded at a pinned version and checked against a SHA-256 written in the
     repository: pinned and checksum-verified, but it runs on the runner host with the runner user's rights,
     so a malicious build could alter `dist/` or the runner's action files before the artifact upload.
   - *The syft container image, pinned by index digest* (`ghcr.io/anchore/syft:vX.Y.Z@sha256:…`), run with no
     network, a read-only root file system, no capabilities, the runner's UID, the inputs mounted read-only
     and only a fresh, empty output directory writable: pinned and checksum-verified by the daemon, with no
     access to the job token, the Docker socket, the network or `dist/`. It is not fully isolated from the
     runner: its output reaches the job log, where lines starting with `::` are workflow commands, so the
     script captures that output in files and prints it only inside a `::stop-commands::` wrap (*Decision*).

   Registry for the pin:
   - *`ghcr.io` only*: the digest is read there and the image is pulled from there; the daemon verifies the
     pulled content against that digest.
   - *`ghcr.io`, cross-checked against the same tag's digest on Docker Hub*: adds no assurance about what
     actually runs (the pull is verified against the pinned digest regardless), is blocked by anonymous
     Docker Hub rate limits, and leaves no defined action on a mismatch (the two registries are published
     separately). Rejected.

   Chosen: the syft container image pinned by index digest, read from and pulled from `ghcr.io` only.
2. **Format**
   - *SPDX 2.3 JSON* (`spdx-json@2.3`): an ISO standard, the format of GitHub's dependency-graph export; the
     version in the output format pins the predicate type `https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`, so the documented
     `--predicate-type` stays valid when syft changes its default SPDX version.
   - *CycloneDX JSON*: equally supported by `actions/attest`; one predicate type for every version.

   Chosen: SPDX 2.3 JSON, with the version written out.
3. **Where the generator runs**
   - *In the `attest` job*: the job that can mint a signing token would run third-party code, against 0054
     (it runs only GitHub's own actions and `gh`). Rejected.
   - *In a separate job between `build` and `attest`*: no job token scope, but the job would have to download
     and re-upload artifacts; a compromised generator with access to the artifact runtime token could replace
     the `release` artifact that `publish-image`, `attest` and `github-release` consume.
   - *As a step of the `build` job, inside the restricted container*: the SBOMs are written before the upload
     and travel in the `release` artifact; the container cannot reach the job token, the artifact service or
     `dist/` (option 1).

   Chosen: a step of the `build` job, through a shared script `.github/scripts/generate-sbom.sh`, which the
   `Release build check` in `ci.yml` runs too, so a broken generator or pin fails in pull-request CI and not
   on a release tag.
4. **Where the SBOM is published**
   - *As SBOM attestations only*, through the GitHub attestations API like the provenance (0054, option 3):
     the document a consumer obtains from `gh attestation verify --format json` is signed and bound to the
     artifact's digest.
   - *Also as release assets*: easier to download without `gh`, but an unsigned copy next to the signed one
     invites using the unverified file, and the image SBOM has no natural place among the binary assets.
   - *Also in Docker Hub* (`push-to-registry`): needs the registry token in the signing job, rejected in 0054.

   Chosen: SBOM attestations only.
5. **Content check before attesting**
   - *None*: an empty or malformed SBOM would be signed and published.
   - *A small check in the script*: `spdxVersion` is `SPDX-2.3`, both documents list the Go standard library
     (`stdlib`) and the main module, the image document lists at least one Debian package (`pkg:deb/`), and
     each file is at most 16 MB.

   Chosen: the check.
6. **Keeping the syft pin current**
   - *Dependabot*: cannot read an image reference in a script; a separate Dockerfile only to expose the
     reference would add a Dependabot `docker` entry and a build step for nothing else. Rejected.
   - *Refreshed by hand*, documented in `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` like the base image digests (0041), with a
     follow-up issue to add the syft pin to the weekly digest report (0080).

   Chosen: by hand, with the follow-up issue.

## Decision

- `.github/scripts/generate-sbom.sh <agent-binary> <image-tar> <version> <dest-dir>` holds the constant
  `ghcr.io/anchore/syft:vX.Y.Z@sha256:<index digest>` (a release tag, never `latest`), checks its form as a
  whole string before use, and runs it twice with `docker run --rm --network none --read-only --tmpfs /tmp:rw,mode=1777,noexec,nosuid,nodev
  --cap-drop ALL --security-opt no-new-privileges --user <runner uid>:<gid>`, the two inputs bind-mounted
  read-only and a fresh empty directory as the only writable mount, each as
  `--mount type=bind,source=<absolute path>,…` (never `-v`, whose `:`-separated form reads a relative source
  as a named volume): `scan file:` for the binary and
  `scan docker-archive:` for the image tarball, output `spdx-json@2.3`, application update check off. It
  copies only the two expected regular files (not symlinks) to `<dest-dir>` as
  `vandox-agent-linux-amd64.spdx.json` and `vandox-image.spdx.json` and checks their content (option 5).
- Before any `docker` call the script makes every path absolute and accepts it only if it matches
  `^/[A-Za-z0-9._/+-]+$` (no `,`, `:` or other character the mount parsers treat specially); the inputs must
  be regular files and not symlinks, the destination a directory, not a symlink, without either SBOM name.
- The container's stdout and stderr (and the Docker CLI's pull output) go to files in a directory that is
  not mounted into the container; the script prints them, and anything else read from an SBOM, only between
  `::stop-commands::<token>` and `::<token>::`, with a random token generated after the container runs, so
  the generator cannot issue workflow commands. `::error::` lines carry fixed text, never SBOM- or
  container-derived strings.
- `release.yml`, job `build`: a step `Generate SBOMs` after `Save image` and before the upload; the two files
  travel in the `release` artifact. `SHA256SUMS` still lists only the binary.
- `release.yml`, job `attest`: unchanged permissions (`id-token: write`, `attestations: write`), no
  environment, no secret, no checkout. Two more `actions/attest` steps at the same pinned SHA, with
  `sbom-path`: one for `dist/vandox-agent-linux-amd64`, one for `docker.io/networlddev/vandox` at
  `publish-image`'s digest; `push-to-registry` stays off. `Verify attestations` also runs both checks with
  `--predicate-type https://spdx.dev/Document/v2.3`. `github-release` still needs `attest`, so no GitHub
  release exists without verified SBOM attestations.
- `ci.yml`, job `Release build check`: saves the image and runs the same script; it uploads nothing.
- `README.md` documents verifying and extracting each SBOM; `docs/CONTRIBUTING.md` documents the release
  steps, the pin and how to refresh it.

## Consequences

- Consumers can obtain a signed SPDX 2.3 SBOM for a release binary or image digest with `gh`, bound to the
  same workflow, tag and runner checks as the provenance.
- The SBOM states what syft found. It is generated in the `build` job, which also runs the Go build and
  `docker build`; an attacker who controls that job can falsify the SBOM as well as the binary, as for the
  provenance (0054). The predicate is workflow-controlled content, not a guarantee by the signer.
- A new third-party tool is in the release pipeline, confined by digest and by the container restrictions.
  A malicious build of that exact digest could still write false SBOMs and noise in the job log, but cannot
  reach the job token, `dist/` or the network, nor issue workflow commands.
- The syft pin ages until it is refreshed by hand; a stale syft gives a less complete SBOM, not a weaker
  release. Follow-up: report the syft pin in the weekly digest workflow.
- `ghcr.io` must be reachable for every release and every `Release build check`; an outage fails both.
- If an SBOM attestation fails, the image is already published, as for any `attest` failure (0054); a re-run
  of `attest` adds a second SBOM attestation for the same subject, which is harmless.
- The attestation path is still first exercised by a real tag; the generation and the content check run on
  every pull request.
